paper_topic: OCR-Anchor Reranking: best-of-N selection for VLM document parsing fails due to candidate homogeneity

nodes.text: Converting PDF documents to machine-readable formats such as Markdown is a critical first step in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and document analytics pipelines.

Vision-language models (VLMs) have emerged as powerful tools for this task, capable of handling complex layouts including multi-column text, tables, and mathematical equations (Blecher et al., 2023; Wei et al., 2024; Poznanski et al., 2025).

However, VLM-based document parsing remains stochastic at inference time, where small decoding differences can cause significant downstream failures such as missing table rows, permuted reading order, or hallucinated content.
Best-of-N sampling has proven effective for improving language model outputs in reasoning tasks (Wu et al., 2024; Chow et al., 2024).
The approach generates multiple candidates and selects the best one using a reward signal, enabling inference-time scaling without retraining.
nodes.display_label: Generate N, select best by reward

nodes.text: For document OCR, this is appealing because it can be applied to any base model as a reliability layer.
The key challenge is candidate selection: the model's own log-probability may not correlate well with visual correctness, and directly comparing long structured outputs is difficult.
nodes.display_label: Selection is hard: logprob, output compare

nodes.text: We propose OCR-Anchor Reranking, a training-free method that uses traditional OCR as a proxy verifier for VLM outputs.
The key insight is that classical OCR engines like PaddleOCR (Cui et al., 2025) can extract high-confidence tokens that serve as visually-grounded anchors, independent of the VLM's language prior.
We score each VLM candidate by the fraction of anchor tokens it contains and select the candidate with highest coverage.
nodes.display_label: Score by anchor coverage; pick max

nodes.text: Our comprehensive evaluation on olmOCR-Bench (Poznanski et al., 2025) reveals a negative result: the method does not improve over baselines.
All selection strategies—including random selection—perform within a 0.3-point band (82.0–82.3%).
The root cause is candidate homogeneity: at low temperature (0.1), 90.6% of pages produce identical candidates across all 8 samples.
When there is no diversity to select from, no selection strategy can succeed.
We propose OCR-Anchor Reranking, a training-free method for selecting among VLM-generated document parsing candidates using traditional OCR as a proxy verifier.
We provide comprehensive evaluation showing that the method fails to improve over baselines, with all selection strategies performing within noise of each other.
nodes.display_label: C2: method fails; all strategies = noise

nodes.text: We identify the root cause as candidate homogeneity at low temperature, where 90.6% of pages produce identical outputs.
We discuss broader implications for best-of-N approaches: the technique requires candidate diversity, which well-trained models at low temperature do not provide.

observations:
FA0115 is a negative-result paper about transferring best-of-N to document OCR. Para 1 is Context (N1-N3) framing PDF→Markdown for RAG and the stochastic-VLM problem — the 'However' in N3 is field-level Context (the topic-of-study is VLM parsing stochasticity, so this is paper-theme alignment). Para 2 introduces Prior_Work (N4-N5) on best-of-N sampling, then transitions back to Context (N6) — the appeal for OCR — and lands on the Limitation N7: candidate selection is hard.

N7 (Limitation) has a Prior_Work source via N4 (best-of-N selection is hard precisely because best-of-N's own selection mechanism — model logprobs — does not work for visual correctness). The N4→N7 contrast edge satisfies Pass 3.

Para 3-4 is the Method (N8-N10): OCR-Anchor Reranking with PaddleOCR. Para 5 is the Result chain (N11-N14): negative finding, all strategies similar, root cause is candidate homogeneity, no diversity → no selection. N14 forks into four Contribution bullets (C1-C4).

Topologically, N14 is the dominant fork. One addresses edge: C1 (proposes OCR-Anchor Reranking) → N7 (the candidate-selection challenge). Although the paper's headline is negative, C1 is still framed as addressing N7 (logprob doesn't correlate, so we propose OCR anchors as alternative selector). C2-C4 are empirical findings about why the addressing fails. Narrative arc: VLMs do PDF→Markdown but stochastically → best-of-N is appealing but selection is hard → propose OCR-Anchor Reranking → negative: all strategies within noise → root cause is candidate homogeneity at low temperature → broader best-of-N needs diversity.
